text: Robert Wu Nov 21, 2026 44 8 5 Share People on my side of the Pacific woke up on Saturday morning to something quite shocking. NASDAQ down more than 5%. Nvidia down a whopping 14%, and the multi-trillion-dollar darling crown-jewel of AI has halved in value in a matter of a few weeks. This is the week we just had, and it’s all about China: Jensen, one of the biggest symbols of modern-day American capitalism, was out because of dealings with the Chinese. The US Commerce Department imposed licensing requirements on shipments of advanced chips to overseas data centers that supply significant computing power to Chinese companies. After the rules changed, TSMC reportedly halted certain advanced orders from Chinese chip designers unless they secured a US license. Many of these orders are not even about AI chips, but even smartphone chips to clients like Xiaomi . Lawmakers are also pushing for tighter controls on chipmaking equipment . The White House and Treasury have discussed making American companies disclose their use of Chinese models . Even the Chinese optical components inside American data centers are now in Washington’s sights. On Thursday, AMD became a new target of attack for potentially undisclosed China sales . If you believe AI is a zero-sum game, you would think all of these efforts would send NASDAQ to heaven. But instead, we now have a market that’s on the verge of collapse in both China and the US. Not many people have talked about the big elephant in the room yet, but let me say it: the US, and especially the Rubio-Dario grouping of interests, has f* up big time. They have vastly underestimated the level of inter-dependency between the US and China in the AI industry. Their gambit to encircle Chinese AI is likely to be the final nail in the coffin for the bursting of its own AI bubble. China is a major client of America’s AI industry. In May, Culper Research estimated that Chinese demand accounted for more than 20% of Nvidia’s fiscal 2026 compute revenue , including demand through Southeast Asian intermediaries and what it alleged was chip diversion. I have heard of estimates putting that number even higher.
